literal_question.instructions: Is the other person's latest message meant purely literally, with no subtext? Judge from the whole thread, not one sentence in isolation.

criteria.true: The latest message is a straightforward statement, question, or plan with no implied accusation, test, sarcasm, hint, or unsaid request.
criteria.false: There is subtext: a test of whether you remember or care, sarcasm, an implied complaint, a hint they will not say outright, a trap question, an accusation dressed as a question, or a cold/short line that really means blame.

true_intent.instructions: What is the other person's true intent in the latest message, given the full conversation? Prefer tone and context over surface wording. If they are checking whether you remember something or still care, choose confirm_you_care even if the words look like a request to 'say it' or to do something. If they already accepted and closed the matter peacefully, choose close_topic. Ending the relationship, deleting you, or 'don't talk to me' is vent_anger, never close_topic.

criteria.confirm_you_care: They are testing whether you remember, pay attention, or still care. Signals: 'did you forget again', 'then say it', 'you better', sarcastic 'busy person', asking you to prove you know a past conversation. If they mainly want a new deliverable or a yes on a time, do not use this.
criteria.vent_anger: They are angry or hurt and mainly want the feeling acknowledged. They are blaming or raising the temperature; a specific plan is not the main point yet.
criteria.request_action: They want a concrete action, time, deliverable, or commitment from you now, and this is a real ask, not a loyalty test.
criteria.seek_explanation: They want a factual explanation of why something happened. They asked why or what is going on, not mainly for an apology or a new plan.
criteria.casual_chat: Light talk, banter, sharing, teasing with a laugh, or friendly logistics with no emotional test and no conflict. A friend suggesting a meal time can be this if the thread is warm.
criteria.close_topic: Peaceful wrap-up only: they accepted an apology, confirmed a happy plan, said thanks, or clearly signaled they need nothing more. Not a breakup, not 'don't contact me', not sarcastic 'I'm used to it'.

danger_level.instructions: How close is this conversation to a fight or to hurting the relationship? Match the current scene. If they genuinely accepted an apology or confirmed a happy plan, score the cooled-down present, not an earlier complaint. If an ultimatum (break up, report to the boss, stop covering for you) is still in force and has not been withdrawn, stay in that high bin even if the latest line names a specific task.
criteria: Light chat or joking; no complaint, no test, no deadline.
Mild tease or a small reminder that is easy to laugh off; a clumsy reply would only feel slightly awkward.
A mild complaint or 'please remember next time' said without heat; they still send warm or practical follow-ups.
Noticeable unhappiness; they mention being forgotten, ignored, or kept waiting, but still give you a chance to make it right.
Sarcasm, cold short replies, or 'you better'; they are testing you, and a sloppy or fake-confident reply will escalate.
Openly upset; they accuse you of not listening or not caring; they expect a real response, not a joke.
Clearly angry and blaming you; a wrong reply will turn this into a fight.
Last-chance warning. They will not cover for you, do not want to keep talking unless this changes, or tell you to finish a named checklist yourself because trust is almost gone.
An ultimatum is already on the table even if they also give a practical next step: break up if you forget again, report you tonight, or stop working together if you miss this.
Active rupture: they said it is over, told you not to reply, deleted you, or are exploding.

should_reply_now.instructions: Should your next message contain substantive content? Substantive means: admitting a specific known fault, giving a concrete time/plan/deliverable, explaining facts you actually know, or reciting the recalled content they asked you to say. This is NOT 'should you send any message'. Timing is irrelevant. Answer FALSE if the thing they want you to recite or prove is not present in this snippet (you would be guessing). 'Then say it' / 'you better' while you are stalling is FALSE. Answer FALSE if they already accepted and closed the topic. Answer true only if the needed fact, plan, or named fault is already in this snippet.

criteria.true: The needed fact, named fault, or named time/place is already in this snippet, and they are waiting for that substance now.
criteria.false: Do not put substance in the next message: the recalled content is not in this snippet, they are testing whether you remember, a holding line is enough, saying less is safer, or they already closed the topic.

best_action.instructions: What type of next action is best? Do not decide whether to send a message immediately. Ignore timing. Choose only the action type. If they asked you to recall a specific past message or event and you have not shown that you actually remember it, choose check_history — do not apologize or invent a plan instead.

criteria.check_history: Look up prior chat or facts before taking a position. Use when they ask you to repeat, recall, or prove you remember something specific.
criteria.apologize: Lead with a sincere apology for a real mistake or hurt already identified. Not for an unnamed forgotten thing when you should first find out what it was.
criteria.give_commitment: Give a concrete promise, deadline, or arrangement they asked for in a conflict or work-pressure setting.
criteria.explain: Explain what happened or why, without leading with apology or a new plan.
criteria.acknowledge: Show you heard them and care, without new facts, an apology, or a plan. Use for light chat or when they mainly need to feel seen.
criteria.say_less: Keep it short or add nothing. Extra words would over-explain, reopen a closed topic, or pour fuel on an ultimatum that told you not to talk.
criteria.make_plan: Propose or confirm logistics (time, place, task) for a non-conflict request such as a meal or a meeting.

she_needs.instructions: What does the other person need from you right now? Judge the LATEST message first. If they genuinely accepted (thanks / got it / 没事了 / 那就这样 / 收到了 / 过去了), you MUST choose nothing, even if earlier they wanted action or an apology. Sarcastic 'I'm used to it', 'whatever', 'I don't want to hear it', 'don't bother coming' is NOT genuine satisfaction — do not choose nothing. If they asked you to recap a named time/place/date, choose action. If they are testing whether you remember or still care, and the content is unnamed, choose care.

criteria.apology: They need a sincere apology for hurt or a mistake, and they have not accepted one yet.
criteria.action: They need a concrete action, time, commitment, recap of a named fact, or follow-through, and they have not yet accepted one.
criteria.explanation: They need a clear explanation of what happened or why, and have not received it.
criteria.care: They need proof you remember, listen, or care — a loyalty or attention test — not yet a plan or an apology. Sarcastic 'I am used to it' belongs here, not nothing.
criteria.nothing: They need nothing further. Genuine acceptance, a peaceful closed topic, warm casual chat with no ask, or a rupture where they told you not to reply. Not sarcasm pretending to be fine.

tension_resolved.instructions: Has interpersonal tension already been resolved? Answer true only if there was never tension, or the other person has clearly accepted, cooled down, joked again, or said it is fine. A sarcastic 'you better', an unanswered test, leftover blame, or an open ultimatum means false.

criteria.true: No remaining tension: they accepted, joked again, said it's fine, confirmed a happy plan, or the chat was never tense.
criteria.false: Tension is still present: they are waiting, testing, angry, sarcastic, issuing an ultimatum, or the issue is open.

addressed_to_me.instructions: In this GROUP chat, is the latest message directed at the user (from=me is the user)? True if they were @mentioned, asked a question only they can answer, assigned a task, or called out by name. False if it is general chatter, a joke to the room, or someone else is being addressed. The state field mentioned_me is a hint from the client, not proof.

criteria.true: The latest line is aimed at the user: an @mention, a named ask, a task for them, or a public call-out.
criteria.false: The latest line is for the group or for someone else. The user can stay silent.

true_intent.instructions: What is the latest speaker trying to do in this GROUP thread? Judge the latest message in context. Do not treat this as a one-to-one romantic chat.

criteria.ask_you: They want YOUR answer, decision, or confirmation, not a generic group reaction.
criteria.assign_task: They are assigning work or asking you (or the room including you) to do something concrete.
criteria.coordinate: Scheduling or coordinating among several people; you may or may not be needed.
criteria.announce: Informing the group. No reply is required unless they asked a question.
criteria.joke: Banter, a meme, or light chat with no task and no call-out.
criteria.call_out: They are criticizing you or putting you on the spot in front of others.
criteria.off_topic: Not directed at you and not needing your input.

danger_level.instructions: How risky is it for the USER to speak or stay silent in this group right now? Score the present scene. Public blame, a work deadline aimed at them, or a fight already started belongs high. Ordinary logistics and jokes belong low.
criteria: Ordinary group noise or a joke; missing one message costs nothing.
Light coordination; a late reply is only slightly awkward.
Someone asked a mild question that could wait.
A task or time is on the table; silence will be noticed but not punished.
They @mentioned the user or asked something only the user knows.
Public pressure: they named the user or implied the user dropped a ball.
Open group conflict; a sloppy reply will make it worse.
The user is being blamed in front of others and needs a careful line.
Work or relationship risk if the user answers wrong or stays silent.
Active pile-on, HR/boss risk, or they told the user not to speak.

should_reply_now.instructions: Should the user send a message NOW in this group? True only if they were addressed, their fact or decision is needed, or staying silent would look like they are hiding. False if someone else is handling it, it is chatter, or they do not have the fact yet.

criteria.true: A short reply from the user is needed now: they were asked, assigned, or publicly called out.
criteria.false: Do not send: not their turn, they lack the fact, or silence is safer.

best_action.instructions: What type of next group message is best? Ignore timing of notifications. If they were not addressed, prefer wait. If a named fact is missing from the snippet, prefer clarify or wait, do not invent.

criteria.reply_brief: A short acknowledgment or one-line answer is enough.
criteria.give_fact: Give a concrete fact, time, or number already present in this snippet.
criteria.volunteer: Offer to take a clearly named task.
criteria.wait: Do not speak yet. Someone else is handling it or the user was not asked.
criteria.clarify: Ask a short clarifying question before committing.
criteria.correct: Politely correct a factual error about the user or the work.
criteria.deescalate: Cool down a group conflict without taking a loud side.

she_needs.instructions: What does the GROUP or the latest speaker need from the USER right now? If they were not addressed, choose nothing. If they asked for a named fact or task, choose action. Public blame that wants an apology is apology. Do not choose care unless they are asking the user to take a stance.

criteria.apology: They want the user to own a named mistake in front of the group.
criteria.action: They want a concrete action, time, or fact from the user.
criteria.explanation: They want a short explanation of what happened.
criteria.care: They want the user to take a visible stance or show they are paying attention.
criteria.nothing: They need nothing from the user. Chatter, someone else's thread, or a closed notice.

tension_resolved.instructions: In this group, is interpersonal tension already gone? True only if there was never tension, people joked again, or the call-out was clearly accepted. An unanswered @mention, leftover blame, or an open work miss is false.

criteria.true: No remaining tension: accepted, joked again, or the thread was never tense.
criteria.false: Tension is still present: waiting, blaming, or the issue is open.

group_register.instructions: What is the social register of this GROUP right now? Use title, relationship, and wording. A family dinner plan is family. A standup or deadline is work. Banter among peers is friends. If mixed, choose mixed.

criteria.work: Workplace, school project, or formal coordination. Titles, deadlines, owners.
criteria.family: Family or household. Parents, relatives, home logistics.
criteria.friends: Friends or a casual club. Jokes, hangouts, no formal owner.
criteria.mixed: Cannot tell, or work and personal are mixed in the same thread.

open_loop.instructions: Is there still an unanswered ask for the USER in this snippet? The state may include open_ask and mentioned_earlier as hints. True if someone asked the user something and from=me has not answered it yet. False if the user already answered, someone else closed it, or there was no ask.

criteria.true: An ask or task for the user is still open.
criteria.false: No open loop for the user, or it was already answered.

reply_target.instructions: If the user sends a message, who should it address? Use latest_speaker when answering the last line. Use earlier_asker when the last line is noise but an earlier ask is still open. Use whole_group only for a short broadcast that must reach everyone. Use nobody if they should not speak.

criteria.latest_speaker: Address the person who just spoke.
criteria.earlier_asker: Address the person who asked earlier and is still waiting.
criteria.whole_group: A short note to the whole group, not one person.
criteria.nobody: Do not address anyone; they should not send, or a nameless line is enough.

thread_status.instructions: What is the current thread doing? new_topic if the latest line starts something else. continue if it follows the same ask or plan. pile_on if several people are stacking on one person. resolved if the ask was accepted or closed.

criteria.new_topic: The latest line starts a different subject.
criteria.continue: Same plan, ask, or task as the recent lines.
criteria.pile_on: Several people are stacking comments or blame on one person.
criteria.resolved: The ask or conflict already landed; nothing useful to add.

rank.instructions: Which candidate reply is the most appropriate next message, given the conversation and the other person's true need? Prefer a reply that matches the best action type. Penalize dismissive, over-promising, or off-topic replies. If the facts are not yet confirmed, prefer the candidate that looks them up instead of faking memory or a vague apology.
rank.group_instructions: Which candidate is the most appropriate NEXT message in this GROUP chat? Prefer a reply that matches best_action. Penalize couple-chat tone, long apologies, @everyone, answering when wait was correct, and inventing facts not in the snippet.
